summary: JWT refresh mid-session causes orphaned function executions and duplicated external webhook calls behind private API gateway
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external webhook invocations and orphaned function call side-effects when their client SDK performs an automatic JWT refresh mid-stream while connected to a Private deployment behind an internal API gateway. Duplicates show up as repeated outbound POSTs to the same webhook with slightly different idempotency metadata.

Impact:
- Customer observed repeated charges in downstream system (payment webhook) for ~12 orders over a 3-hour window.
- Affects single customer cluster in their Private deployment (FinVault production cluster).
- Risk: financial reconciliation and potential regulatory exposure.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment (v2025-12-03) on customer-managed VPC
- Customer SDK: python-sdk v0.9.8 (auto-refresh enabled)
- Ingress: internal API gateway (company-managed) performs header cleaning and routing to Redwood private control plane
- Network: mTLS with short-lived JWTs (60s TTL) rotated by auth service

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Start Python streaming session using function-calling (sdk.generate_stream with tools enabled) to orchestrate a checkout flow.
2) Mid-stream (~35s in) customer auth service returns a refreshed JWT via a background refresh and client replaces Authorization header on the socket without reconnecting.
3) SDK continues the stream; outgoing function call triggers an external webhook.
4) Customer sees the webhook endpoint receive 2–3 POSTs for the same logical action within seconds.

Observed behavior:
- Outbound webhook requests include an idempotency header that appears truncated or normalized differently by gateway (e.g., idempotency-token: "ord-9f8c..." vs "ORD-9F8C...").
- Server logs show the same request being retried in the runtime with overlapping request IDs after the JWT swap.
- Webhook server reports duplicate processing for 11/12 of the events.

Expected behavior:
- Mid-session JWT refresh should be transparent to the runtime and SDK without causing duplicate function invocations or replays.
- Idempotency tokens must be preserved verbatim across proxied requests so downstream systems can deduplicate.

Logs / snippets provided by customer:
- client debug logs (python): "Refreshed JWT, swapping Authorization header mid-stream, resuming socket"
- runtime snippet: "received_request id=3a7b... parent_stream=st-99a; kvcache_hit=false; resume_token=tok-44"
- gateway access logs show header-normalization rule: lowercase-all-headers=true

Additional context:
- Customer is on a Private deployment with custom gateway header sanitation rules.
- They intentionally rotate JWTs aggressively for compliance.
- They use our function-calling pattern where each \"tool\" maps to an external webhook with downstream non-idempotent side-effects (billing).
comments: 2026-03-01 09:12 - Support (Aisha Malik): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE and Eng. Added P1 and requested logs + replay instructions. Asked customer to pause webhook processing as a mitigant if possible.

2026-03-01 10:03 - SRE (Priya Shah): Noted gateway header-normalization. Hypothesis: header canonicalization is modifying idempotency token case/format causing runtime to treat calls as different or SDK to retransmit. Also possible: mid-stream auth header swap triggers a transport-level reconnect and SDK retry logic replays function call without de-dupe metadata. Collecting tcpdump and runtime request traces.

2026-03-01 14:36 - Customer (FinVault - ops@finvault.com): Provided tcpdump, gateway config snippet, and example webhook POSTs. Confirmed gateway lowercases header names and strips unknown header characters. Asked for recommended immediate mitigation.

2026-03-02 08:21 - Engineering (Diego Alvarez): Reproduced locally with private-like proxy that lowercases headers and short JWT TTL. Observed that when Authorization header is swapped in-band, the SDK's internal stream library flips to 'soft-reconnect' mode which resends the last tool invocation after re-establishing the control frame. Instrumentation shows runtime receives duplicate tool invocation frames with different request_meta.idempotency_value (case-normalized). Opened PR to make SDK preserve idempotency metadata at the application layer and add stronger dedupe on runtime if idempotency token exists header-agnostically.

2026-03-02 15:00 - Support (Aisha Malik): Shared temporary mitigation: configure gateway to passthrough our idempotency header (x-redwood-idempotency) and disable header normalization; or increase JWT TTL to avoid mid-stream rotation. Customer applied passthrough rule and reported immediate reduction in duplicates.
investigation:
Findings:
- Reproduction succeeded when proxy lowercases header names and removes non-alphanumeric characters, which modified the idempotency token case and occasionally truncated hyphens.
- SDK behavior: during an in-band Authorization swap the underlying websocket/stream client transitions modes, and because function-call acknowledgement had not yet been observed by the client, it retried the tool call. The SDK retry used the in-memory idempotency token which had been normalized by the gateway (case changed), so downstream webhook saw a different token.
- Runtime mitigation gap: runtime deduplication currently checks idempotency tokens using case-sensitive equality on headers; when headers are mutated by proxies, the runtime cannot dedupe.
Hypothesis validated by: reproducing with a local envoy config that lowercases headers and forces a header rewrite mid-stream.
Next steps proposed:
1) Short-term: recommend customers set gateway passthrough for x-redwood-idempotency and/or increase JWT TTL. Support to provide config snippets ASAP.
2) Medium-term (ENG): SDK patch to include idempotency token inside the streaming control frame payload (application-level) so proxies cannot mutate it; PR opened: serving-runtime/pull/2124 and python-sdk/pull/486.
3) Long-term (ENG): runtime to implement case-insensitive idempotency header normalization and token canonicalization (strip non-alphanum preserved characters) and stronger single-source dedupe keyed by request-id + canonical token.
resolution_notes:
Workaround implemented and validated:
- Customer updated their gateway to passthrough x-redwood-idempotency and disabled header lowercasing for requests to the private control plane.
- Customer temporarily increased JWT TTL to 5 minutes to avoid mid-stream refreshes during active sessions.
Permanent fix plan:
- Merged python-sdk change to embed idempotency token in control frames (python-sdk v0.9.9).
- Serving runtime PR (idempotency canonicalization + case-insensitive compare) merged to main; will ship in v2026-03-15 scheduled private deployment patch.
Follow-ups:
- Post-deploy validation runbook created and linked: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/JWT+Rolling+Keys+Runbook (added a checklist item about idempotency passthrough).
- Customer will run a canary for 48h after patch; Support to monitor billing webhook traffic and confirm no duplicates.
Status: In Progress (workaround applied; permanent fixes merged and scheduled).
resolution: Workaround applied; permanent fixes merged and scheduled for deployment
customer_impact_summary: Duplicates caused 11 duplicate webhook-side charges affecting 12 orders. Mitigated by gateway passthrough and TTL increase; awaiting runtime + SDK rollout for full remediation.
